findings.message: The new PM card's pin is keyed on the project key (`args: { key: project.key }`). R3/059 says a record's PinRef names it by UUID, and `get_project` declares `pin: { id: "projectId", ... }`. Delivery already builds this pin the right way in `projectPin()` (modules/delivery/pins.ts:16, `args: { projectId: p.id }`), so this is also a second copy of that logic that disagrees with it. Fix: use `args: { projectId: project.id }`, or expose `projectPin` through delivery's contracts and call it here.
findings.scenario: Someone pins the TMT PM card, then the project's key changes or the key is reused. The pin no longer resolves to the same project, or resolves to a different one.

findings.message: The monthly extend job reads the open standing rows without locking them. It then inserts month rows and moves `filled_to`. If `setStanding` ends or replaces the same standing at the same time, the end deletes month rows and commits first, and the extend then writes new rows after the end. Fix: read with `select ... for update` (or lock the standing row in both writers) and check `until_month is null` again before inserting. Add a test that runs the two writers at the same time.
findings.scenario: On the 1st at 02:00 the extend transaction reads Dinesh's open CON standing. A PM ends it from 2027-01 (percent 0, standing) and commits. The extend then inserts 2027-11 at 50%, so Dinesh is still allocated to CON after the end.

findings.message: "A month set by hand wins" only works for months that have a row, because it relies on `on conflict do nothing`. A month someone removed by hand (percent 0 deletes the row) and that lies past `filled_to` leaves no trace, so a later extend writes the standing percent into it. Fix: keep removals past `filled_to` as an exception (for example a zero row or a skip list on the standing) that the extend respects.
findings.scenario: A standing from 2026-11 at 50% is filled to 2027-10. The PM sets 2027-12 to 0 (no row exists, so nothing changes). On 2027-01-01 the extend writes 2027-12 at 50%, so the person's 'not on it that month' is lost.

findings.message: The standing path skips the `before` snapshot that the month path records. `setStanding` deletes up to 12 hand-set month rows, or every row from `month` on when it ends a standing, and the audit row holds no record of what was removed. Fix: select the rows it will delete (same slot and range as the deletes in setStanding) and return them as `before.rows`, as the month path does.
findings.scenario: Tharushi has 2027-06 set by hand to 25% on CON. allocate(standing, percent 0, month 2027-05) deletes 2027-05 onward. The audit row shows only `after: { from: 2027-05, percent: 0 }`, and the 25% month is gone with no record.

findings.message: `percent: z.coerce.number().int()` turns null, false, "" and "  " into 0, and percent 0 means 'remove'. Before this change the MCP tool used `z.number()` and refused those values. Chat's form removes empty fields before parsing, but a raw MCP call does not. Fix: preprocess only non-empty numeric strings, for example `z.preprocess((x) => typeof x === "string" && x.trim() !== "" ? Number(x) : x, z.number().int())`.
findings.scenario: An MCP client sends `{ person: "Kasun Dias", projectKey: "CON", percent: null }`. It parses as percent 0, and Kasun's CON allocation for this month is deleted instead of the call being refused.

findings.message: The retention clock for `allocations.standing` starts at `from_month`, so a standing that is still open is anonymised 7 years after it began. Its `person_id` and `updated_by` are rewritten while it still drives the monthly extend. Fix: start the clock at `until_month` (and keep open rows out of the purge), or at `updated_at`.
findings.scenario: An internal-project member has stood on the project since 2026-11. In 2033-11 the purge anonymises the row's person_id. The next extend writes allocation rows for the anonymised id, and the real person drops off the team.

findings.message: add_person now silently links the new HR record to any active sign-in that has the same work email and no HR record yet. Neither the confirm card nor the audit's `after` says that a sign-in will be linked. A mistyped or reused email gives another account self-service access to this person's employment and pay data. Fix: show 'Links to <account name>' on the card (addPersonCard) and record `userId` in the audit `after`, or ask for the link explicitly.
findings.scenario: HR adds Priya with workEmail it-admin@lumenlabs.test, an admin account with no HR record. The record is linked to it-admin, who now sees Priya's employment record as their own, and the card never said so.

findings.message: AC-3 says the month row wins for its month. setStanding does the opposite. It deletes every existing allocation row in the 12-month window, including months someone set by hand, and writes the standing percent over them. Ending a standing allocation (percent 0) also deletes hand-set rows after that month. Only the monthly extend job respects hand-set months, through `on conflict do nothing`. Fix: on set, insert with `on conflict do nothing`, or delete only rows written by an earlier standing allocation. On end, delete only rows that standing allocations wrote. The test at standing-107.test.ts:25 currently asserts the destructive behaviour.
findings.scenario: Dinesh is hand-set to CON at 10% for 2026-12. Then allocate {person: Dinesh, projectKey: CON, month: 2026-11, percent: 50, standing: true} runs. The 2026-12 row is deleted and rewritten at 50%. The hand-set 10% is lost.

findings.message: This loosens the 106 final-pass NO_FORM refusal: a draft tool whose input fully parses can now be proposed with no form. The diff has no engine test for it. Add a table test over three cases: draft-only input with no form is refused; full input with no form is proposed; draft input with a form is proposed.

The `ProjectRef` contract gains `billing` (and `EVENTS.projectManagerChanged`), but the README's contract notes don't mention the `billing` addition. The module standard asks for a README note when a contract that other modules use changes.

set_project_manager accepts any active user, but the `@managed` project rights come from the PM role's grants. If the new manager has no PM role, they get none of the PM rights (AC-1: 'gets the project's PM rights at once'). The old PM also loses managed scope, so only an Admin can still manage the project. Fix: refuse a user who has no PM or Admin role assignment, in both proposeManager and the service, and add a variant test for an Engineer target.
findings.scenario: Maya (PM) runs set_project_manager {projectKey: TMT, userId: <Kasun, Engineer>}. The write succeeds. Kasun cannot move proposals, record deployments or hand the project back. Maya has lost @managed on TMT. No PM can manage TMT any more.

findings.message: The Who chips use the person's name as the value (`value: p.name`). personOf refuses a name that matches more than one person ('matches more than one person; use the employee number'). The card's own picks can therefore never be confirmed when two active people share a name. Fix: use `p.employeeNo` as the chip value and keep the name in the label, so the button label still reads the name.
findings.scenario: Two active people are both named 'Kasun Perera' and neither is on CON. Both chips have the value 'Kasun Perera'. The person picks one and confirms, and the confirm is refused with 'matches more than one person'.

findings.message: proposeAllocate runs raw SQL on `auth.user` from inside the allocations module, outside any contract or `@amax/auth` function. It also checks HR existence under a job context rather than the viewer's scope. The pre-check can then pass for someone the service's viewer-scoped `personOf` later refuses with a different error. Fix: read the account through an `@amax/auth` function, and check HR with the same context `setAllocation` uses.
findings.scenario: A PM whose HR scope doesn't reach person X names X. propose passes because the job context sees X. At confirm the service fails with 'no person X' rather than the field message.

findings.message: Month rows the extend job writes emit no `allocations.allocation.set` event. Webhook and outbox consumers see a standing allocation's first 12 months but none after that. Either emit an event per extended slot, or document that consumers must read `standing: true` as open-ended.
findings.scenario: A webhook subscriber that mirrors allocations stops receiving rows after month 12 of a standing allocation.
